changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/12032-approval-requests-data-source.md`

- names `apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` → `apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` — edited by this change

  > - **`ApiDataSource.findOne` resolves `null` only on a 404.** Every other failure (a 403, a 5xx, a transport error) now rejects, the way `ObjectStackAdapter.findOne` does. Before, any failure resolved `null`, so a record page over a `provider: 'api'` source showed a refused or failed read as "Record not found". It now shows "no access", or "could not load" with Retry (the record page states from objectui#11902). - **A console data source for approval requests.** `apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` routes reads of `sys_approval_request` to the approvals routes through `ApiDataSource`, and everything else to the console's own adapter. Each source serves one server-side scope: awaiting me, submitted by me, or all. Rows come back as the approvals service serves them, so `viewer` and (on a single read) `decision_progress` are fields a view can bind. On a list read, `$top`, `$skip` and `$search` become the route's `limit`, `offset` and `q`, and `$select` is dropped. Every other parameter, such as a filter, a sort or an expansion, is refused with an `UNSUPPORTED_QUERY_PARAM` error, so the list shows its error panel and never shows unfiltered rows. Nothing mounts the source yet; the approvals list and detail pages that will use it come later.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `2312bd9a6` (merge-base with origin/main): 28 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 430 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (446 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/38536757385)

### ① Derived judgments

Published-surface reach first: no `exports` map and no entry barrel changed in any of the seven packages between base and head. Every change below is reachable through an unchanged barrel, so it IS on the published surface where named.

1. `@object-ui/core` `resolveDataSource`: `case 'api'` deleted; an `api` block now takes the `default` arm (fallback, else `null`). **Right** — this is the first reader the ruling names, and the test pins it as identical to an unknown provider.
2. `@object-ui/core` `ResolveDataSourceOptions` loses `fetch` and `defaultHeaders` (published via `adapters/index.ts`). Only the deleted arm read them; kept, they would be inert accepted members, which ADR-0049 is the rule against. A caller passing `{ fetch }` as a literal now gets TS2353 (the dev's reverse validation). **Right, and within the ruling** — the option members were the reader's only input, not a separate feature. Narrowing of a published type: belongs in core's bump (see ②).
3. `@object-ui/core` `ViewDataProvider` (file-surface extension): `case 'api'`, `resolveApi`, `extractRecords` deleted; `ViewDataConfig` loses the `api` member, `ResolvedData.provider` narrows to `'object' | 'value'`, `DataFetcher.fetchUrl` removed. `ViewDataProvider`, `ViewDataConfig`, `DataFetcher`, `ResolvedData` are all published through `data-scope/index.ts`. This is a second reader of the same retired arm (a `case`, not a `provider === 'api'` compare, so the card's grep missed it); `fetchUrl` was called only by `resolveApi`. **Right, within the ruling**; `Type Check` green on this head is the evidence no in-repo `DataFetcher` literal still supplies `fetchUrl`.
4. `@object-ui/core` `ApiDataSource`: class, `ApiDataSourceConfig` (still carrying `read`/`write`/`fetch`/`defaultHeaders`) and its export from `adapters/index.ts` unchanged; only the docblock and the missing-config error string ("Ensure the ApiDataSourceConfig has read/write configs.") move. **Right** — the ruling's "keep the approvals inbox's code-built `ApiDataSource`" holds; `apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` changes a docblock only, and the inbox tests are inside the green `Test` shards.
5. `@object-ui/react` `useViewData`: no `apiFetch` threading, no `api` keying in the memo; `adapterOptions` stays typed `ResolveDataSourceOptions`, so it inherits the narrowing in 2. The pin shows an `api` block falls back to the context DataSource and requests its URL through no channel. **Right.** `SchemaRendererContext.apiFetch` itself is untouched (it still serves other channels) — nothing deleted beyond the reader.
6. `@object-ui/plugin-gantt` `ObjectGantt`: `api` branch out of `adapterInputsKey`, `apiFetch` out of the adapter memo and both effect dependency lists, drawer `needsRealRecord` and `onRefresh` no longer branch on `api`; `ObjectGanttProps` unchanged. **Right** — the three sites the card named at `:832`, `:2064`, `:2585`, nothing more.
7. `@object-ui/plugin-list` `ListView`: `ganttOwnsData` and its skeleton guard deleted, so a gantt list with an `api` block fetches its bound object like any list. **Right** — these are the card's `:1605` / `:2381` sites; the test flips to the new meaning. The `data` pass-through to the gantt schema stays, so no `object`/`value` block is dropped on the way.
8. `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` / `@object-ui/plugin-map` (file-surface extensions): the `dataProvider === 'api'` branches that only `console.warn`ed and committed an empty set are deleted; an `api` block now falls off the `else if` chain exactly as an unknown provider does. No prop or type changes. **Right**; these would be TS2367 against spec `main` once core compiles, so the extension is the same defect class, as the dev declared.
9. `@object-ui/types`: `objectql.ts` docblocks only; `ViewData`, `HttpRequest`, `HttpMethod` re-exports stay, `objectql.zod.ts` untouched. **Right** — `HttpRequest`/`HttpMethod` are the shape `ApiDataSourceConfig` is built with, so they have a non-view reader and stay (this answers the card body's open question on the `HttpMethodSubsetSchema` / `HttpRequestSchema` re-exports, which the PR body does not state outright; the green `Spec Main Shape Gate` shows spec `main` still exports both).
10. Docs (`plugin-gantt.mdx`, `plugin-map.mdx`, core adapters README, gantt README) stop prescribing the arm and say what an `api` block now gets. Prose face, outside the three contract faces; read sentence by sentence, consistent with the code.
11. Nothing deleted beyond the ruling: `ApiDataSource`, `ApiDataSourceConfig`, `SchemaRendererContext.apiFetch`, the `'DataSource required for object/api providers'` error text, the `HttpRequest` types and every barrel are intact.
12. `Clause-②: no` — **right**. The diff accepts no new key, widens no schema and adds no export; every change removes a reader or narrows a published type. A narrowing, which is why this review exists.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/12325-retire-api-view-data.md`: `minor` for core, react, plugin-gantt, plugin-list; `patch` for plugin-calendar, plugin-map, types, console. objectui AGENTS.md §9 (version-alignment rule): objectui's own breaking changes ship as `minor` with the break spelled out in the body, and `major` only on the sync bump that follows an @objectstack major; `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces it and `Changeset Bump Policy` is green.

- core `minor`: **matches**. Published types narrow (`ResolveDataSourceOptions`, `ViewDataConfig`, `ResolvedData.provider`, `DataFetcher.fetchUrl`) and behaviour changes for an `api` block — breaking, which under the policy is `minor`, and the body spells the break out.
- react `minor`: **matches** (`useViewData` behaviour and the inherited `adapterOptions` narrowing).
- plugin-gantt and plugin-list `minor`: **match** (behaviour of an authored `api` block changes; no type-surface change, but the policy's `minor` is the right bump for a behaviour break).
- plugin-calendar and plugin-map `patch`: **acceptable**. No published type changes; an `api` block drew nothing and requested nothing before and does the same now; the only difference is the lost dev-facing `console.warn`. Declaring `minor` would also have been defensible; `patch` is not wrong.
- types and console `patch`: **match** — docblock-only source edits in fixed-group packages.

Under the policy no entry could be `major`, and none is. The levels declared match what is removed.

Each is a reader (or a test riding on the reader's default) of the same retired arm, declared in the PR body with the reason the claim's grep missed it, and the goal of the ruling (the gate green while objectui still runs it) is not met without them: `Spec Main Shape Gate` is `success` on this head.

They are not readers and this card does not own the bump; the carrier is the PR that moves objectui onto a `@next` refusing `api`, and that PR must flip them. None of these is a reader and none changes the accept set, so they do not block this PR; but the two zod `describe()` strings are published prose that still names the retired arm to authors, so one follow-up card should carry all of them. Not this PR's file surface.
